newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks $5 billion for school construction.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks $5 billion for school construction.

text.p: President Clinton Thursday called for the creation of a $5 billion federal fund to help needy school districts repair aging buildings as part of his fiscal 1998 budget proposal.

"The fund would support interest subsidies or similar assistance to cut borrowing costs for states and localities in order to reach higher levels of infrastructure investment," the White House said in budget documents released today.
The General Accounting Office found recently that a third of all U.S. schools, with 14 million students, have one or more buildings needing extensive repair, the administration pointed out.

"School districts also face the cost of upgrading schools to accommodate computers and modern technology, and of constructing new classrooms and schools to meet expected record enrollment levels over the next decade," the administration said.
"The President proposes to leverage new construction or renovation projects through a $5 billion fund for school districts with substantial need," it said.
